samples.summary: Two other "exit the list" paths still hardcode 'paragraph', bypassing `unlistedBlockType`
samples.evidence: `Doc.splitBlock` at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:298-300 (`if (block.type === 'list-item' && blockText.length === 0) this.setBlockType(blockId, 'paragraph')`) and `Doc.deleteBackward` at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:263-265 both leave a list by forcing `'paragraph'`. These are the Enter-on-empty-bullet and Backspace-on-empty-bullet exits, the most common way a user leaves a list. After this change, exiting a bulleted Heading 2 via the toolbar restores the heading while exiting via Enter/Backspace silently destroys the remembered level (and `setBlockType('paragraph')` deletes `headingLevel` outright, so it is unrecoverable). The `unlistedBlockType` doc comment claims it keeps the exit behaviour from drifting across implementations, but these two model-layer exits were not routed through it. Fix belongs at document.ts:264 and :299 (call `unlistedBlockType(curBlock/block)`), not in the diff.

samples.summary: Splitting a bulleted heading drops the remembered level on the tail block, so sibling bullets un-list to different types
samples.evidence: `applySplitBlock` at packages/docs/src/store/block-helpers.ts:256-258 does `if (newBlockType !== 'heading') delete after.headingLevel;`, and the Yorkie tree path mirrors it at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2139-2141 (`newBlockType === 'heading' && block.headingLevel !== undefined`). Pressing Enter inside a bulleted heading therefore yields two visually identical list items where the first un-lists to Heading N and the second to a paragraph. The todo doc (docs/tasks/active/20260816-docs-unlist-restores-heading-todo.md:50) lists this as a non-goal, so it may be deliberate — but the inconsistency is now user-visible and lives entirely outside the diff.

samples.summary: Slides text boxes inherit the new un-list behaviour through @wafflebase/docs with no slides-side consideration or test
samples.evidence: packages/slides/src/view/editor/text-box-editor.ts:625-627 forwards `toggleList` straight to the docs `initializeTextBox` API (imported at line 25/34), whose `toggleList` is one of the three sites changed here (packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1122). Slide text-box blocks are stored as full `Block[]` (packages/slides/src/model/element.ts:265), so a slide bullet made from a heading now round-trips back to a heading inside a slide placeholder. Nothing in the slides package or its suite covers this cross-package behaviour change.

samples.summary: Toolbar style label consumer makes the retained heading level invisible, so un-bulleting looks like a spontaneous type change
samples.evidence: `getBlockLabel` (packages/frontend/src/components/text-formatting/text-style-options.ts:112) and `blockTypeToStyleId` (:127) both gate on `type === 'heading'`, and `blockStyleId` maps `list-item` → `'normal'` (packages/docs/src/model/named-styles.ts:111-112). While the block is a bulleted heading the toolbar reads "Normal text"; toggling the bullet off then jumps the label to "Heading 2" with no prior indication that state existed. These consumers still work but are now inconsistent with the model.

samples.summary: Markdown autoformat "- " applied on a heading now leaves a hidden heading level behind
samples.evidence: packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2317-2323 converts the current block to `list-item` on typing "- "/"* " without clearing type-specific state; with the new retention in `MemDocStore.setBlockType`/`YorkieDocStore.setBlockType` a heading turned into a bullet this way silently keeps its level, so a later bullet toggle produces a heading the user never asked for. This call site was not considered by the change.

finding.summary: Two other "exit the list" paths still hardcode 'paragraph', bypassing `unlistedBlockType`
finding.evidence: `Doc.splitBlock` at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:298-300 (`if (block.type === 'list-item' && blockText.length === 0) this.setBlockType(blockId, 'paragraph')`) and `Doc.deleteBackward` at packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:263-265 both leave a list by forcing `'paragraph'`. These are the Enter-on-empty-bullet and Backspace-on-empty-bullet exits, the most common way a user leaves a list. After this change, exiting a bulleted Heading 2 via the toolbar restores the heading while exiting via Enter/Backspace silently destroys the remembered level (and `setBlockType('paragraph')` deletes `headingLevel` outright, so it is unrecoverable). verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. `Doc.deleteBackward` (document.ts:263-265) and `Doc.splitBlock` (document.ts:298-300) both exit an empty list-item by calling `setBlockType(..., 'paragraph')`, bypassing the new `unlistedBlockType` helper (types.ts:337-344) that the three toolbar `toggleList` sites now use (editor.ts:2870, text-editor.ts:2169, text-box-editor.ts:1125). `MemDocStore.setBlockType` retains `prevHeadingLevel` only for the `list-item` branch and otherwise does `delete block.headingLevel` (memory.ts:249-262), so exiting via Enter/Backspace permanently destroys the remembered heading level while the toolbar exit restores it. Both paths are reachable from real key handling: Enter at text-editor.ts:798-804 -> handleEnter -> docSplitBlock (2049/2082/2105) -> doc.splitBlock; Backspace at text-editor.ts:780-787 -> handleBackspace -> doc.deleteBackward (1933). No intercepting guard exists in the view layer. This is a blast-radius issue: consumers of the changed contract left inconsistent, major impact.
